chapter-01.question: What makes a maintained source useful for multiple outputs?
options: It is written in Markdown
The handbook, training material, and other outputs use the same maintained sources
It is stored on GitHub
Every output has the same layout
chapter-01.feedback: Reuse depends on explicit relationships and processing, not on a file format or platform.

chapter-01.question: Which statement best describes Document-as-Code?
options: Replacing all documents with code
Applying versioning, review and processing to maintained information
Publishing every file as a website
Using AI to write all procedures
chapter-01.feedback: The approach applies software-style discipline to information; it is not tied to one output or tool.

chapter-02.question: A contributor makes a Git commit. What is established by that action alone?
options: The change is approved
The website is updated
A revision is recorded
All checks succeeded
chapter-02.feedback: A commit records a revision. Review, automated checks and publication are separate.

chapter-02.question: Which tool records commits and branches?
options: Git
Astro
Markdown
GitHub Pages
chapter-02.feedback: Git is the version-control system; GitHub hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration tools.

chapter-03.question: Why record a source revision in a generated report?
options: To prove its content is approved
To connect the report to its inputs
To increase the commit count
To replace validation
chapter-03.feedback: A recorded revision supports provenance; it does not itself prove correctness.

chapter-03.question: An AI agent proposes changes to an access procedure and two related guides. What should reviewers examine?
options: Only the access procedure, because the guides cover the same topic
The diffs across all three files, checking that the instructions remain consistent
Only the agent's summary, because it describes the intended changes
Only the build results, because successful checks establish consistency
chapter-03.feedback: Review the actual changes across all affected files. A summary or successful build alone does not establish that the instructions remain consistent.

chapter-04.question: Which Markdown line creates a top-level heading?
options: # Access instructions
- Access instructions
**Access instructions**
[Access instructions](#)
chapter-04.feedback: A leading # followed by a space denotes a level-one heading.

chapter-04.question: Why can Markdown help with reviewing changes?
options: It automatically approves edits
Its plain-text source can be compared in a diff
It prevents duplicate information
It always generates multiple documents
chapter-04.feedback: Text-based source can be inspected and compared; approval and reuse require other practices.

chapter-05.question: In a procedure file, what does 'owner: onboarding-team' describe?
options: The team that made the most recent edit
The team responsible for maintaining the procedure, not necessarily the team authorized to approve it
The team that approved the latest revision
The team responsible for running the validation program
chapter-05.feedback: The owner is responsible for maintaining the procedure. Who may approve it is a separate decision in the team's review process; ownership alone does not grant approval authority.

chapter-05.question: How do frontmatter and YAML relate in the procedure example?
options: Frontmatter checks the fields, while YAML approves the procedure
YAML is used only inside Markdown frontmatter
Frontmatter is the opening metadata block; YAML is the format used to write its fields
Frontmatter contains the instructions, while YAML controls their appearance
chapter-05.feedback: Frontmatter describes the block's position and purpose. YAML is a structured text format that can also be used in separate files.

chapter-05.question: You enter 'status: unknown' in the practice file and select Validate metadata. Why does the check fail?
options: The schema allows only draft or approved as status values
Unknown is invalid YAML syntax
GitHub permits only approved procedures
The source file must be committed before it can be checked
chapter-05.feedback: Unknown is valid text in YAML, but it is outside the status values allowed by this practice schema. The validator applies that rule when you run the check.

chapter-05.question: Two procedure files each pass the single-file practice schema and both use PROC-003. What else must be checked?
options: Whether their headings use the same Markdown level
Whether identifiers are unique across the selected records
Whether both files use approved as their status
Whether their previews look identical
chapter-05.feedback: A single-file schema cannot compare its identifier with other files. Cross-file processing must check uniqueness across the selected records.

chapter-06.question: Which item should remain identifiable if a procedure is renamed?
options: Its stable ID
Its display title
Its file position
chapter-06.feedback: A stable identifier allows relationships to survive a title change.

chapter-06.question: Why distinguish a procedure link from an activity prerequisite?
options: Both mean the same thing and can use the same label
A procedure link identifies guidance; a prerequisite identifies something that must happen first
A procedure link proves the activity has been completed
chapter-06.feedback: Relationships have different meanings. Guidance identifies instructions used by an activity; a prerequisite identifies a dependency, not proof of completion.

chapter-07.question: A successful processing run necessarily means the resulting handbook is approved.
options: True
False
chapter-07.feedback: Automated processing and human content approval are separate.

chapter-07.question: You edit the Contacts text and see the change in its preview, but the generated handbook still has the old wording. What updates the handbook?
options: Validate the Contacts metadata without rebuilding
Run checks and build successfully using the edited source
Change the Contacts status to approved without rebuilding
chapter-07.feedback: The preview follows the editor immediately. The handbook is a separate generated output: it changes after the configured checks pass and the build combines the current sources.

chapter-08.question: What is the distinction between a chat prompt and an AI agent?
options: A prompt gives instructions; an agent combines a model with tools whose access and actions depend on its configuration
Naming a repository in a chat prompt is enough for the model to read its files
An agent is simply a longer prompt containing more background information
chapter-08.feedback: A prompt describes the task; it does not grant access. An agent can retrieve sources or run checks through configured tools and permissions. A chat interface can also provide those tools: the distinction concerns the system's capabilities, not how its interface looks.

chapter-08.question: An agent updates a procedure and its build passes. What provides a basis for accepting the change?
options: The passing build alone establishes that the instructions are accurate
Reviewing the diff and generated outputs alongside the check results
The agent used versioned sources, so its changes need no further review
chapter-08.feedback: The build verifies configured processing, while the diff and outputs make the change inspectable. Reviewers use that evidence to assess meaning and suitability before acceptance.

chapter-09.question: What gives the connection between Processing and Metadata its meaning in the knowledge graph?
options: The distance between the labels in the 3D view
The recorded relationship: Processing uses Metadata
Their labels having the same colour
chapter-09.feedback: The relationship records how the concepts connect. Positions and colours help you navigate the view; the named relationship carries the meaning.

chapter-09.question: How can an AI agent use the graph to explain how the onboarding lab builds its review queue?
options: Treat each line as a complete explanation
Follow the relationships and reading references, then use the chapter text to explain the example with sources
Infer every relationship from the position of the labels
chapter-09.feedback: The Metadata → Processing → Derived view route helps find the explanation. Chapter 7 shows how the status field is used to select drafts for the queue.

chapter-10.question: The Astro pull-request check succeeds. What has happened to the published website?
options: Nothing from this check: it validates the proposed site without deploying it
GitHub Pages now serves the pull-request version
Every chapter has been approved
chapter-10.feedback: The PR workflow checks a proposed change. A separate workflow deploys from main; passing checks is not content approval.

chapter-10.question: The PDF proof workflow uploads a successful artifact. Where is the proof available?
options: In that workflow run's retained artifacts; it is not automatically published on Pages
As a new public PDF book on GitHub Pages
Inside the Markdown source of every chapter
chapter-10.feedback: Actions artifacts and GitHub Pages are different destinations. The limited proof is downloadable while retained, subject to GitHub access requirements.

chapter-11.question: You select Metadata in the knowledge graph. How does its description appear?
options: Astro prepares the data at build time; JavaScript in the browser displays the selected concept
GitHub Pages runs the Python record processor on every click
The browser rewrites the maintained Markdown records
chapter-11.feedback: The build prepares the concept records. Browser code uses those records to respond when you select a label; an edited source description reaches readers after a new build and deployment.

chapter-11.question: A team maintains procedures in Word and SharePoint. Which practice from this tutorial can it apply?
options: Agree on the maintained source, preserve its history and define how changes reach readers
Keep a separate editable copy for every use of each procedure
Assume that storing a file in a library completes its review
chapter-11.feedback: The tools can differ while the team still maintains a shared source, inspects changes and defines a path to the reader.

chapter-12.question: What is lost when a team saves only a chart rather than its underlying dataset and calculation method?
options: The choice of chart colors
The ability to verify, reproduce and extend the analysis
The original chart title
The possibility of making a PDF
chapter-12.feedback: Keep the original records, calculation rules and notes so a colleague can check the result and update it when more information arrives.

chapter-12.question: What can we conclude from the three usable durations in this example?
options: Team A resolves cases faster than Team B
Every case took six days to resolve
These three cases have a median duration of six calendar days
The two cases left out of the summary are still open
chapter-12.feedback: The middle value of 3, 6 and 7 is 6. All three usable durations belong to Team A; missing or reversed dates leave the other two durations unresolved.
